porque.quienes: Osppy is a Corporate AI consultancy: we put artificial intelligence to work inside your company's operation.

como.headline: Understand first. Building is the last step.
como.p1Body: Discovery and viability: we get to know your operation and identify where AI genuinely helps, and where it isn't needed.
como.p2Body: Data evaluation and audit: what information exists, where it lives and how ready it is for a system to work with it.
como.p3Body: The process gets written down and the solution is drawn on top of it, with a scoped proof of concept (PoC) before building at scale.
como.p4Body: Development of the system and of its technical operation (MLOps). Quoted separately, with written scope and success criteria: you measure the impact, with your own numbers.
como.p5Body: Governance and retraining: what we deliver stays under a monitoring and maintenance plan, and the system adjusts as your operation changes.

voces.headline: What it feels like to have a system doing the work.
voces.q1: What changed wasn't the tool. It was that we finally wrote down how a quote gets made, and then it could be automated.
voces.q2: I thought it would be another chatbot. It's a step of the process nobody does by hand any more.
voces.q3: They told us one area wasn't worth it yet. That conversation is what made us trust them.

faq.headline: What people usually ask us.
faq.q1: Does this work at a company with many areas?
faq.a1: Yes, and that's where it pays off most, but you don't go in through all of them at once. You start with one area and one task, leave it running, and that becomes the example the rest of the company understands it by.
faq.a2: Almost always with a diagnosis: understanding your operation and identifying where AI genuinely helps. What follows depends on what shows up: training, tidying up a process, or building a system.
faq.q3: What if our processes aren't written down anywhere?
faq.a3: That's the most common case. Structuring the process is part of the work, and it comes before any automation. We don't build agents without well-defined processes.
faq.a4: It doesn't promise savings, sales or hours: your numbers measure that. It doesn't hand over a tool and walk away. And it doesn't build systems that decide for your team: artificial intelligence proposes, a person reviews and decides.
faq.q5: What happens to my company's information?
faq.a5: We define in writing what information may be used, what gets anonymized and what stays out. And AI tools do get things wrong: that's why everything is built so a person can review and decide.
faq.a6: Training and advisory are quoted per group and per result; builds separately, with written scope and success criteria. We don't publish prices because we don't sell packages: every proposal is about your case.
faq.q7: Does it connect to my systems?
faq.a7: Yes: they connect to the ERP and the invoicing system you already use. Which ones exactly, and how far the connection goes, is settled in the diagnosis, by name, before it appears in a proposal. We don't promise an integration we haven't checked against your system.

hero.headline: Diana answers your hotel's WhatsApp at any hour. Diana books for you, and you manage it.
hero.sub: A front desk with artificial intelligence: it answers with your hotel's real information, quotes, builds the complete reservation, confirms it and handles everything before, during and after the stay. Behind it there's a panel where your team sees everything and operates from one place.
hero.nota: Osppy's assistant operates today in hotels in production · On the official WhatsApp API from Meta

labels.setup: How do you get set up?

root.answer: Hi 👋 I'm Diana, Osppy's assistant for hotels. I live in your hotel's WhatsApp: I answer guests with your information, quote them, build their reservation and follow up until they leave. And I let you know about whatever needs your decision. Ask me anything.

different.answer: I'm not a menu of options. I understand a long message with three questions mixed together and answer all three, in Mexican Spanish or in English if that's what I'm written in. And if something isn't loaded, I say so or ask: I never make up a rate or a policy.

pricing.answer: It's billed monthly, per property. There are different plans depending on how many conversations your hotel has, plus a one-time setup. You'll get the numbers at the demo, with your case in front of you.

night.answer: Yes. At three in the morning on a Sunday I answer the same as on a Tuesday at noon.

setup.answer: You hand us rates, policies, rooms and the questions you get asked most; the Osppy team loads it, registers the templates with Meta and tests everything end to end before going live. It takes days, not weeks.

human.answer: Whenever you want. From the panel you see every conversation, take over, and when you resolve it I pick it back up. And if I detect a complaint or anything sensitive, I hand it to someone on your team right away.

demo.answer: Great. Book a demo and I'll show you how I'd answer at your hotel, with your rates and your policies. A person will take care of you.

problema.headline: Overnight messages go cold. Daytime messages are always the same.
problema.body: A small hotel lives off direct bookings on WhatsApp, and that WhatsApp almost always lives on the phone of whoever runs the place. This is how it sounds from the inside:

r1.titulo: They write at one in the morning
r1.body: “They ask the price and whether breakfast is included, and by the time I answer they've booked somewhere else.”

r2.titulo: Answering the same thing twenty times
r2.body: “Price, breakfast, parking, check-in time. The same thing, all day, at any hour.”

r3.titulo: A number that never switches off
r3.body: “My WhatsApp lives on my personal phone and I can never disconnect. And the direct booking slips away because nobody answered in time.”

hace.headline: Answers with your information. Builds the reservation. You approve.
hace.body: Diana replies on your hotel's WhatsApp with what you loaded: rates, taxes, cancellation policies, breakfast, pets, parking, check-in and check-out times and your frequently asked questions. Whatever isn't loaded, it doesn't make up.

i1.titulo: Quotes and builds the complete reservation
i1.body: Dates, room, number of guests and name, in the same conversation. Multiple rooms or the whole property too, with extra-person charges and taxes as you defined them.

i2.titulo: Hands it to you with a button
i2.body: The built reservation lands on your WhatsApp with two buttons: approve or decline. On approval, Diana sends the guest the deposit details. The room is taken when it's paid, not when it's approved.

i3.titulo: Hands over to a person when it matters
i3.body: Complaints, sensitive requests or anything outside its remit reach your team with a heads-up. From the panel someone answers and resolves it, and Diana picks the conversation back up.

conversacion.m1: Hi, do you have a room for two people from Friday to Sunday? Is breakfast included, and do you have parking?
conversacion.m2: Hi! Yes, for those dates we have a double room for two. Breakfast is included and there's free parking for guests. I'll send you the rate with taxes included, no surprises. Shall I set up the reservation?
conversacion.m3: Yes please. Do you take pets?
conversacion.m4: Yes, small pets with a per-stay fee; I'll include it in the total. To build the reservation I just need your full name.
conversacion.m6: Done, Andrea: double room, Friday to Sunday, two people. I'm passing your reservation to the hotel; as soon as they approve it I'll send you how to make the deposit. Your room is held once the payment comes in.

circuito.headline: Diana does it. You approve with one tap. The panel shows it all.
circuito.sub: Nothing confirms itself. Diana does the work: quotes, builds the reservation, sends the deposit details and confirms with the guest. You manage it: approve and confirm payment with one tap.

funciones.headline: What it does, and what it deliberately doesn't.

f1.body: Rates, taxes, policies, breakfast, pets, parking, schedules and your FAQs: loaded once, in your own words, and that's what Diana answers with.

f2.body: At night and on weekends it answers just like at noon, with the same information and the same tone.

f3.body: Mexican Spanish by default. If the guest writes in English, it answers in English and stays in that language.

f4.body: Approve or decline from your own WhatsApp, without opening anything else. And if two people ask for the same room, whoever pays first keeps it: there are never two paid reservations on the same room.

f5.body: Complaints, sensitive requests or topics outside its remit it doesn't answer: it passes them to your team with a heads-up and picks back up once someone resolves them.

f6.titulo: On the official WhatsApp API from Meta
f6.body: Meta-approved templates, privacy notice on first contact, one-word opt-out, data isolated per business and daily encrypted backups off the server.

widgets.chatA1: Yes, there's a pool for guests. Want me to send photos?

no.n1: It doesn't connect to booking platforms or reservation systems: not today, and with no committed date.
no.n2: It doesn't confirm reservations on its own: it always goes through your button.
no.n3: It doesn't offer discounts or room upgrades on its own initiative.
no.n4: It doesn't replace your team: it takes the repetitive part and leaves them the decisions.

arranque.headline: Days of setup, not weeks of project.
arranque.p1: You give us your information: rates, policies, rooms, amenities and your most repeated conversations, so Diana speaks in your vocabulary from day one.
arranque.p2: Osppy loads the configuration, writes and registers the templates with Meta and tests the full loop.
arranque.p3: We hand you the panel with role-based access and run the kickoff session with your team.
arranque.nota: The clock is set by Meta's verification of your number, not by the setup work.

precio.headline: One structure, no fine print. The figures, on your case.
precio.body: We don't sell flat packages. The real cost of the service is driven by conversation volume, and a flat price ends up degrading the service: we'd rather say so up front.
precio.p1: A monthly fee per property, with a fair-use allowance of conversations included.
precio.p2: Different plans depending on your hotel's number of conversations; you see the volume in the panel.
precio.p3: A one-time setup: loading rooms, policies, FAQs, templates and testing.
precio.p4: Several properties in a single account.
precio.p5: No long contracts. Your data is yours and exportable.
precio.nota: You get the figures at the demo, with your volume and your operation in front of you.

testimonios.headline: What it's like to have the front desk answering on its own.
testimonios.q1: I used to answer messages at midnight every single day. Now I sleep.
testimonios.q2: I thought a bot would feel fake. My clients write to it the same way they write to me, and it knows when to hand the conversation over.
testimonios.q3: I stopped losing bookings to slow replies. What comes in overnight no longer goes unanswered.

faq.headline: What a hotel asks us before starting.
faq.q1: What if Diana tells a guest something wrong?
faq.a1: It only answers with what you loaded. If something isn't there, it says so or asks; it never makes up an amenity, a policy or a rate. And it never confirms a reservation on its own: that always goes through your button.
faq.q2: Does it connect to my reservation system or to the platforms?
faq.a2: Not today, and we won't give you a date we can't keep. That's why the lock is you, with the approve buttons: for a small hotel it's the healthiest way.
faq.q3: Do I have to change my WhatsApp number?
faq.a3: You decide. Your current number can move to Diana (it stops working in the phone app and old chats don't migrate), or you use a new one and keep yours as it is. We look at it together based on how you use it today, and the clock is set by Meta's verification.
faq.a4: Diana runs on the official WhatsApp API from Meta, with approved templates. Blocks come from unofficial setups.
faq.q5: Does it replace my front-desk staff?
faq.a5: No, and that's not what we're selling you. It takes away the grind of answering the same thing twenty times a day. The decisions stay yours, and handing the conversation to a person is a permanent part of the design.
faq.q6: What if I want to cancel?
faq.a6: No long contracts. You take your data with you: it's yours and exportable.

cta.headline: We'll show you Diana with your hotel's information.
cta.body: You write to us, a person answers, and together we look at how Diana would answer at your hotel. No commitment.

capacitacion.headline: Your team leaves knowing how to use AI in their own work.
capacitacion.body: Live workshops, by group, using the tasks your team already does.
capacitacion.ctaMessage: Hello, I would like to talk about AI training for my team.
capacitacion.metaDescription: Hands-on artificial intelligence workshops for owners, managers and teams, with real tasks from your operation.

queEs.p1: Live workshops, by group, with real tasks from your business. Artificial intelligence is not taught in the abstract: what gets taught is how to do one task of the job faster, more clearly and more safely.
queEs.p2: First we teach people to use the tools well. Then we look at which problems keep coming back, and only then is it worth talking about leaving something running.

paraQuien.q1Body: Judgement to decide where AI is worth using, what to buy, and what not to delegate.
paraQuien.q2Body: A method to standardise, supervise and sustain the use of AI inside their area.
paraQuien.q3Body: Concrete routines for doing the everyday tasks better.

rutas.intro: The routes run in parallel; they are not a ladder. You come in through yours.
rutas.r1Body: A short talk for leadership and a starting workshop for the whole team, from zero.
rutas.r2Body: Workshops by area and by role: documents, photos and voice notes; spreadsheets for sales, receivables and operations; sales and quotes; customer service; administration, invoicing and collections; purchasing and suppliers; field operations; human resources and internal knowledge.
rutas.r2Estado: Prepared with your operation when you book it.
rutas.r3Body: For whoever decides and whoever sustains the use in their area: where AI is worth it and where it isn't, how to get it actually used, safe use and internal policy, and training an internal owner for it.
rutas.r3Estado: Prepared with your operation when you book it.
rutas.r4Body: For people already using it every day: automating repetitive tasks without programming, and designing a knowledge assistant for their area.
rutas.r4Estado: Prepared with your operation when you book it.
rutas.continuosBody: A monthly clinic where you bring the work that eats your time, and a workshop built with examples from your own industry.
rutas.nota: Training is delivered, booked and scheduled today. How finished the material is varies from one workshop to the next, and we tell you before booking, not after.

hecho.t1Body: Getting a whole team working with an enterprise-grade AI tool, with order and rules of use.

encaja.body: Training is the Exploration phase of the method: we get to know your operation and identify where AI genuinely helps, and where it isn't needed. While the team learns to use it, the problems that really do repeat come into view.
encaja.enlaceTitulo: The next phase is the diagnosis

precio.body: Training is priced per group and per result, never per hour.
precio.cierre: The figures come in the first conversation.

faq.a1: The length follows the scope, not the other way around: it follows what the group has to leave knowing how to do. It is written into the proposal, along with the scope and what gets delivered.
faq.q2: Can we practise with the company's real information?
faq.a2: We practise with fictional, public or anonymised information. If you decide to use real data you need internal authorisation, and passwords, banking details, sensitive personal data and full customer databases stay out.
faq.q3: Does a workshop leave my process automated?
faq.a3: No. A workshop teaches capabilities. If a problem worth solving with a system shows up at the end, it is quoted separately, with written scope and success criteria.
faq.q4: Which tool do you practise with?
faq.a4: With Claude, which is Osppy's initial recommendation. The principles carry over to other tools, and that is said in every workshop.

cierre.titulo: Tell us about your operation and we will find where to start.

asesoria.headline: Before building anything, understanding where.
asesoria.body: A first session to diagnose the operation, to identify where artificial intelligence helps and where it is not needed.
asesoria.ctaMessage: Hello, I would like to talk about an advisory session for my company's operation.
asesoria.metaDescription: A diagnosis of the operation to identify where artificial intelligence fits, and where it does not yet.

creemos.headline: AI is worth it when it does a whole task, under written rules, with someone reviewing it.
creemos.c1Titulo: A whole task, not a slice
creemos.c1Body: Half an automated task leaves a person finishing it by hand and checking twice as much. If it can't be done end to end, it isn't time yet.
creemos.c2Body: The system does what the process says. If the process lives in one person's head, the first thing we deliver is the process, not the system.
creemos.c3Body: These tools get things wrong and sometimes make things up. That's why everything is built so someone can review it: the AI proposes, the person decides.
creemos.nota: Technology can take away repetitive tasks; the decisions, the attention that matters and the responsibility stay with people.

diagnostico.body: The first session looks at how you work today, area by area, and identifies where artificial intelligence helps and where it is not needed. It ends with the scope in writing, or it ends with a no.
diagnostico.preguntasTitulo: The diagnostic starts with questions like:
preguntas: Where does your team's time actually go?
Which process repeats the same way every week?
What information do you already have that nobody is using?
What's worth automating, and what isn't yet?

salidas.s1Body: There is an area with one concrete task that repeats, that can be done end to end, and we know which one it is.
salidas.s2Body: The area is the right one and the process lives in one person's head. So the first thing delivered is the process, not the system.
salidas.s3Body: Sometimes the answer is: not yet. We tell you that too.

estructuracion.body: The groundwork: getting the process written down before automating anything. Without it, we don't build agents.

encaja.body: Advisory is the Diagnosis phase of the method: what information exists, where it lives and how ready it is for a system to work with it. Once the process is written and the scope defined, implementation follows.

precio.body: Advisory is quoted separately, with written scope and success criteria.
precio.cierre: The figures come in the first conversation.

faq.q1: How long does a diagnosis take?
faq.a1: It follows the size of the operation and how many areas are in scope. It is written into the proposal before we start, along with what gets delivered.
faq.q2: And if it turns out not to be worth it?
faq.a2: Then that is the answer and you get it. A diagnosis that can only end in a project is not a diagnosis.
faq.q3: Does the advisory commit me to building with you?
faq.a3: No. What comes out of the diagnosis is delivered in writing and it is yours. If you decide to build, that is quoted separately.
faq.q4: What kind of company is it for?
faq.a4: For companies with separate areas, where the work already passes through several hands. There is no fixed list: it changes with the industry, the team, the size and the processes you already have.

cierre.titulo: Tell us which area you want to start with.

implementacion.headline: Systems that stay working inside your operation.
implementacion.body: Agents, assistants and process automation that stay running, with scope and success criteria in writing.
implementacion.ctaMessage: Hello, I would like to talk about implementing artificial intelligence in my operation.
implementacion.metaDescription: Agents, assistants and process automation that stay running inside the company, with scope in writing.

agentes.body: An agent does a whole task on its own, inside a defined process and under written rules. Whole means end to end: half an automated task leaves a person finishing it by hand and checking twice as much.
agentes.revision: The AI proposes; a person reviews and decides. Everything is built so that review is possible.

diagrama.pie: The step almost nobody has written down is the second one.
diagrama.alt: Four-step diagram: the task goes through a process someone wrote down, an agent runs it, and it produces a result.

construido.f1i1Body: They do a whole task on their own, autonomously, inside a defined process, with written rules.
construido.f1i2Body: They answer and attend with the information the business loads. If something isn't there, they say so or ask; they don't make things up.
construido.f1i3Body: Once it is written, the process stops being done by hand: the system runs it and a person reviews the result.
construido.f2i1Body: Systems that put a quote together using the business's own rules and prices, so it doesn't depend on one person.
construido.f2i2Body: Documents that go out to a client are built with your format, your letterhead and your details, without being redone each time.
construido.f2i3Body: The file is assembled as things happen, not the week the auditor arrives, and every document ends up where someone will look for it.
construido.f3i1Body: When the information can't leave your house, the model is deployed inside your own infrastructure, with Amazon Bedrock.

conecta.body: What we build connects to the ERP and the invoicing system you already use. How far that connection goes is defined in the diagnosis and put in writing before it appears in any proposal.
conecta.nota: We do not publish system brands. Naming one requires an instance already delivered, and that is a conversation, not a page.

fases.f1Body: The process gets written down and the solution is drawn on top of it, with a scoped proof of concept (PoC) before building at scale.
fases.f2Body: Development of the system and of its technical operation (MLOps). Quoted separately, with written scope and success criteria: you measure the impact, with your own numbers.
fases.f3Body: Governance and retraining: what we deliver stays under a monitoring and maintenance plan, and the system adjusts as your operation changes.

despues.body: What gets delivered can stay under an operation plan: hosting, monitoring and maintenance.

precio.body: Implementation is quoted separately, with written scope and success criteria.
precio.cierre: The figures come in the first conversation.

faq.q1: What if my process isn't written down anywhere?
faq.a1: That's the most common case, and it is the first piece of work. Writing the process comes before any automation: we don't build agents on top of processes that only live in someone's head.
faq.q2: Does my company's information leave my infrastructure?
faq.a2: It depends on what we build, and it is defined in writing before we start: what information can be used, what gets anonymised and what stays out. When it can't leave, the model is deployed inside your own infrastructure.
faq.a3: What we deliver stays under a monitoring and maintenance plan, and it adjusts as your operation changes. We don't hand over a tool and walk away.
faq.a4: It follows the scope, and the scope comes out of the diagnosis. Before that, any date would be invented, so we don't give one.
